RECREATION AREA HOURS
The state recreation area is open daily from
7 a.m. to 10 p.m. for use year-round.
TRAIL USE
The Turtle Mountain State Recreation Area
has over 12 miles of motorized and
non-motorized trails open to off highway
vehicles (OHVs), hiking, biking,
showshoeing and horseback riding.
Remember to share the trail and practice
good trail etiquette.
PETS ON LEASHES
Pets are welcome but must stay on a
leash while in the state recreation area.
EMERGENCY INFO
In an emergency dial 911.

REGISTRATION
Registration is required to operate any OHV on public lands. North Dakota Residents
must register through the North Dakota Department of Transportation.
Non-residents must purchase a non-resident public trails and lands access permit.
Permits can be purchased at any North Dakota state park, by phone at 701-328-5357
or online at travel.parkrecnd.com.
TRAIL RULES
1. Individuals under the age of 12 may not operate OHVs on public lands.
2. OHV state safety certification card required for operators ages 12-15.
3. Helmets are required for operators and passengers age 17 and under.
4. Must have functioning spark arrestor and exhaust.
5. All OHV use is restricted to designated areas and trails.
6. Driver must obey all posted signs and traffic regulations.
7. Operator must be able to provide proof of liability insurance coverage.
FIRE PREVENTION TIPS
1. Be sure chains and other metal parts aren’t dragging from your vehicle.
2. Check your tire pressure. Driving on an exposed wheel rim can cause sparks.
3. Stay on trails and avoid riding/parking in tall grass. Hot exhaust pipes can start fires.
4. Never let your brake pads wear too thin; metal on metal makes sparks.
5. Make sure your spark arrester is installed and free of carbon build up.
6. Carry a shovel and a water source or fire extinguisher when operating in high or
extremely high fire conditions.
